 In 1977 as the president of the DC Young Democrats, I introduced the resolution that led to the Young Democrats of America endorsing DC statehood at its national convention  in Miami.  That was the first national Democratic Party organization to endorse DC statehood.

responses.topThreeActions:
Using culture as a tool for Statehood advocacy.
As Executive Director of Long Live GoGo and Co Founder of Free DC Project, I’ve helped lead and produce Statehood-focused cultural activations—from GoGo-powered demonstrations and Art All Night Statehood stages to national moments like the DNC—centering DC residents and our lived experience while making Statehood visible, accessible, and undeniable.
responses.intendedActions:
Use my platform to publicly and consistently defend DC autonomy, not just when it’s politically convenient.

Work in partnership with advocacy organizations to mobilize residents, educate voters, and activate cultural spaces around Statehood.

Push for formal resolutions, hearings, and public education efforts that keep congressional interference visible and unacceptable.
responses.congressResponse:
Mobilizing residents and partner organizations for rapid-response actions, public statements, and demonstrations.

Working with advocacy partners to elevate the issue nationally, ensuring congressional interference becomes politically costly—not normalized.

Congress should never be allowed to quietly override the will of DC residents.
responses.partners:
Free DC Coalition – I am a co-founder and active organizer, working daily with partners to defend Home Rule and respond to congressional attacks.

DC Council and the Mayor of the District of Columbia – I intend to work in close partnership with the DC Council and the Mayor to present a united local front against federal interference, coordinate responses to congressional attacks, and ensure Statehood and Home Rule remain core priorities of the District’s elected leadership.

State-level parties and national Democratic partners – I will collaborate with state-level Democratic parties and national party leaders to continue elevating DC Statehood as a democracy and civil rights issue, building off existing relationships developed through national advocacy, coalition work, and presidential election cycles.

Use music, art, storytelling, and public space as entry points to civic education.

Create opportunities for residents to take ownership of the fight, whether through advocacy days, creative campaigns, or local organizing efforts.

responses.additionalComments: DC Statehood is not symbolic to me—it’s personal. I believe Home Rule and Statehood are fundamental to racial justice, democracy, and dignity for the nearly 700,000 people who call this city home. I have spent my career fighting this fight with my whole heart, and I will continue to do so with urgency, creativity, and accountability.

2) Organizing this Free DC Slate to make sure we have a Democratic party that fights against the status quo, pushes other Dem parties to stop voting against us, and supports statehood beyond just talk

responses.topThreeActions:
1. Co-chairing the Free DC Welcoming working group, expanding the volunteer base and engaged participation in Free DC
2. Participating in dozens of Free DC rallies, protests, meetings, and community activities, especially in response to and during the federal occupation
3. When speaking with people from out-of-state, including examples like customer service over the phone, I always ask whether the person has heard of DC statehood, and spend a minute sharing why I support statehood with them.
responses.intendedActions:
Like the rest of the Free DC Slate, I would bring the Free DC spirit of organizing, energy, and resolve that has helped protect Home Rule so far to the Democratic State Committee. The DC Democratic Party should be actively organizing with all statehood-focused organizations like Free DC, 51 for 51, DC Vote, and DC for Democracy, co-hosting events, raising awareness, and partnering on actions to push back on the ongoing attacks on Home Rule. I will lead and support efforts to do this if elected. 

In interactions with other states' Democratic Party organizations, I will never fail to bring up the urgency of statehood. For too long, the DC Democratic Party has been a social club, rather than another tool to organize and raise the issue of statehood across the country.

Finally, I'll respect the will of the DC voters. When organizations like the DC Democratic Party use their power to actively work to undermine sound ballot initiatives passed by an overwhelming majority of DC residents, it looks like a contradiction undermines the case for Home Rule and Statehood. I will never compromise the integrity of our shared goal of Statehood for the People of DC if elected.
responses.congressResponse:
I will continue to participate in protests and other actions to bring political pressure to Congress, whether organized with Free DC or otherwise, with additional resources and relationships with Democratic Party officials as an elected member of the Democratic State Committee. 

I will also use my voting power on the Democratic State Committee to put pressure on our DC elected officials to not obey in advance, and use every tool available to delay, slow, or block federal attempts to interfere with DC sovereignty.
responses.partners:
Free DC. I have been part of Free DC since its inception in mid-November 2024. I have strong relationships with the Free DC founders and leadership through my ongoing participation and leadership on the Welcoming working group. 

The D.C. Statehood Compact, where I have volunteered. An evolution of Students for D.C. Statehood, an organization I volunteered for in and after college, the Compact works to encourage officials across the United States to commit to supporting DC Statehood in the event of further federal legislation or a proposed constitutional amendment.

The DC Council. I have relationships with multiple councilmembers from my political and campaign activities, as well as on policy issues through my work supporting housing affordability and sustainable transportation in the District.
responses.voterInvolvement:
Foster collaboration and cross-pollination between the Party and grassroots organizations like Free DC. That means building a truly collaborative and positive relationship, so we can take actions like co-hosting events, sharing each other's resources and materials, and learning from each other's experiences and perspectives in strategy meetings around Statehood and Home Rule advocacy. 

The Free DC Slate understands that the fight for Statehood will never be solved if our largest political organizations, like the DC Democratic Party, continue to operate in a silo, rejecting the will of DC voters because in situations like I-83 because it may upset incumbents. Statehood will necessarily involve a mass people-powered grassroots movement, as Free DC and other organizations have worked to start building. The Democratic State Committee's elected representatives must work from that same point of view.
responses.additionalComments:
Washington, DC is the only home I've ever known. With democracy under attack by MAGA extremists, the rest of the country is waking up to what Washingtonians have known for our entire lives -- freedom and self-determination are not to be taken for granted. 

Growing up in the District is the best thing that ever happened to me. I am deeply grateful to my family for putting down roots here, and I look forward to doing the same. I know in my bones that we will see Statehood in our lifetimes, because of the incredible work people are doing right now to defend Home Rule in its darkest hour.

responses.topThreeActions: Organized office visits in the Wilson building with Free DC to demand the Mayor and Council reign in federal agents' overreach in DC. Synthesized and shared talking points for residents discussing how the federal law enforcement surge makes DC less safe. Successfully campaigned against repealing SVA in DC FY2026 budget.
responses.intendedActions: As a committee member of the DC Democratic Party, I will pitch DC Statehood to national Democrats as a key priority for the Party moving into 2028. Statehood for DC and Puerto Rico should be at the front of every Democratic candidate's platform, and those who oppose it should be rightfully branded as cowards who look down on the people and fear true democracy. Only with this kind of messaging, bold and consistent, over and over, can we hope to turn DC Statehood from a pipe dream to a political reality.
responses.congressResponse:
DC's government often assumes a defensive stance, carefully crafting laws to preemptively avoid Congressional interference. When we do this, we teach Congress that we fear them, and that they can control us - merely by the threat of their interference.

I would want to flip the script on this, and teach Congress a different lesson. Every congressperson works in DC, and they should not get to go into work and vote against our people without having to see us and hear from us. I would respond to Congressional attacks by rallying our Local officials and leaders in organizations like Free DC and ACLU DC. I would call for a united front and mass, visible resistance - protests, call-ins, sit-ins, press conferences, the whole menu. By making our presence on Capitol Hill constant, consistently voicing our demands, and showing a united front, we can convince Congress that messing with DC is more trouble than it's worth.
responses.partners:
Free DC. Renewed campaign for DC Home Rule and Statehood. Joined in March of 2025 and have been co-chair of the DC Local Government Working Group since July.

DeFlock DC. Grassroots campaign against mass deployment of surveillance technologies in DC. Joined in November 2025.
responses.voterInvolvement: I believe the path to DC Statehood is paved with mass, sustained public pressure. I would invite all DC voters and residents to be a part of paving that path, whether by formally joining a campaign like Free DC, or by participating in smaller ways - going to a protest, or calling Congress, or having conversations with family and friends about why DC Statehood matter. I would promote and create opportunities to participate in this fight, for example by observing or testifying at hearings, attending demonstrations, or visiting Congressional offices.
responses.additionalComments: Our fight for Statehood must not stop at that word. Our Party needs to provide a vision for what DC as the 51st state would look like. True freedom requires expanding healthcare; food and housing justice; funding schools and childcare; keeping our air and water clean; and investing in true violence prevention, not just more cops. All of that needs to be included in our pitch for DC Statehood.

responses.topThreeActions:
As Chair of the DC Democratic Party, I successfully led the passage of a resolution in which Democratic Party leaders from all 50 states and the territories pledged their support for advancing DC Statehood. One of the greatest barriers to statehood is the lack of public awareness outside the District. To address this, I helped develop and distribute educational materials to state party leaders across the country to deepen their understanding of the urgency and importance of statehood, and encouraged them to share this information with their members.

Additionally, we launched the Statehood Speaks podcast, featuring local and national leaders discussing why DC Statehood matters and how we can build broader national support. I also relaunched the Kennedys-King Dinner, elevating it into a national platform that highlights influential leaders and amplifies the call for statehood. Finally, at the 2024 Democratic National Convention, we hosted a DC Statehood educational booth to engage attendees from across the country, educate them on the importance of statehood, and demonstrate how protecting democratic rights in DC strengthens freedoms for all Americans.
responses.intendedActions: Promoting statehood and protecting home rule begins with sustained education and engagement beyond the District. I will continue building on the strong foundation laid by statehood advocates by developing innovative outreach efforts, expanding partnerships with state parties, and equipping supporters nationwide with the tools they need to advocate for DC Statehood in their own communities. Increasing national awareness and support is essential to securing lasting change.
responses.congressResponse: Congressional interference in DC’s local affairs is unacceptable, and we must respond with coordinated advocacy and public pressure. The DC Democratic Party has launched digital advocacy campaigns to mobilize Americans across the country to contact their members of Congress and urge them to respect DC’s autonomy and home rule. I will continue expanding these efforts while encouraging residents and advocates to engage in grassroots advocacy—whether through organizing, contacting elected officials, rallying, or community education. Protecting DC’s right to self-govern requires sustained, collective action, and I am committed to leading that fight.
responses.partners: DC Vote, DC Democratic Party, and all DC Statehood Advocacy Groups
responses.voterInvolvement:
I will continue to involve DC voters and residents in the fight for Statehood by expanding opportunities for education, engagement, and direct participation. Building on initiatives like the Statehood Speaks podcast and our educational outreach, I will ensure residents have access to clear, accessible information about what statehood means and how it impacts their daily lives, rights, and future.

I will work with our local Democratic committees, community organizations, and neighborhood leaders to host forums, town halls, and events that empower residents to learn more, ask questions, and become active advocates. I will also continue using major platforms like the Kennedys-King Dinner and national gatherings to elevate the voices and stories of DC residents, ensuring their experiences remain central to the statehood conversation.

Most importantly, I will support efforts that give residents meaningful ways to participate—whether through voter engagement, grassroots organizing, or sharing their stories with national audiences. The fight for statehood belongs to the people of DC, and I am committed to ensuring they remain informed, energized, and at the forefront of this movement until full representation and equality are achieved.
responses.additionalComments: Democrats have a tremendous opportunity to win big in the next election cycle, and we must be prepared to seize this moment. The DC Democratic Party is hiring an Organizing Director to harness the energy and momentum from our local efforts and channel it into supporting Democratic victories across the country this November. Now more than ever, we need you to get involved and be part of this movement to elect Democrats and strengthen our democracy.

responses.additionalComments:
Op‑Ed from the desk of Stuart Anderson
For generations, DC residents have carried the responsibilities of citizenship without receiving its full rights. We pay federal taxes, serve in the military, raise families, build communities, and contribute to the nation’s economic and cultural life — yet our ability to govern ourselves remains subject to the whims of Congress. That contradiction has always been unsustainable, but today it is impossible to ignore.
The right to self‑governance is not an abstract principle for the people of Washington, DC — it is the foundation of our daily lives. With unprecedented attacks on Home Rule and the continued denial of full Congressional representation to more than 700,000 residents, candidates for public office must be unequivocal about where they stand. Defending our existing rights is non‑negotiable, and advancing statehood is essential to securing a future where DC residents have the same democratic protections as every other American.
This moment demands more than sympathetic rhetoric. It requires a concrete, public commitment to safeguarding the autonomy DC residents already exercise and expanding the rights we have been denied for far too long. Any candidate seeking to lead this city should be prepared to articulate — and act on — a clear plan for strengthening our democratic standing.
To that end, candidates should commit to:
Defending Home Rule against congressional interference by publicly opposing any attempt to overturn locally passed laws, budgets, or criminal‑justice reforms.
Advancing DC statehood as a core policy priority, including supporting federal legislation and mobilizing regional and national coalitions that treat statehood as a civil‑rights issue.
Protecting the integrity of local elections by ensuring that DC’s voting systems, ballot access, and election administration remain under local control and free from federal manipulation.
Educating residents and national audiences about the real‑world consequences of disenfranchisement — from budget delays to overturned laws — and elevating the lived experiences of DC residents who bear those burdens.
Taken together, these commitments form a baseline — not an aspiration — for anyone who claims to represent the people of the District of Columbia. Our fight for equality is not symbolic. It is about the daily dignity, safety, and self‑determination of every person who calls DC home.

It might sound cheesy, but these are core values that we must each connect with in order to co-create the reciprocal trust and accountability needed to deliver the Douglass Commonwealth that we the people of DC need and deserve.

responses.topThreeActions:
My proudest action for statehood has been winning Initiative 83. While I83 was primarily a voting rights measure, it was really a battle over who controls DC's democracy — and it proved that when DC residents organize and fight back, we can win. I collected nearly 400 valid signatures across all eight wards, rebuilt the campaign website in NationBuilder to supercharge our organizing, and volunteered across Ward 1 — tabling, canvassing, and working a polling place on Election Day. We overcame lawsuits, disinformation, and signature challenges. It passed with nearly 73% of the vote, including a supermajority in all eight wards and nearly 80% in Ward 1. Most DC races will use ranked-choice voting this June because of that work.

Second, I ran and was elected as a Ward 1 Dems precinct representative in Precinct 22. Too many of my neighbors had never heard of this position or why it matters. Filling that seat was my way of showing up — and it's why I'm now running for State Committeeman.

Third, I've been building the grassroots infrastructure that statehood will require. Through my work with Free DC, I've trained as a statehood advocate and helped lay the foundation for a five-year campaign that runs through 2030 — timed to capitalize on what we expect will be a Democratic trifecta in 2029. If history repeats itself and Democrats retake Congress and the presidency, we need to be ready. That means doing the work now: identifying allies, mobilizing donors and volunteers, and making sure the right candidates win up and down the ballot between now and then.
responses.intendedActions:
My entire focus as State Committeeman will be on winning statehood by the end of my four-year term. Here's how:

Build the grassroots movement. I'll partner with Ward 1 organizations — religious groups, recreational sports leagues, restaurants, bars, and neighborhood associations — to meet people where they are. Statehood passed with more than 89% support in Ward 1 in 2016. People are passionate about this issue; they just need guidance on how to help. I'll make sure those on-ramps exist, with options that match varying levels of time and money.

Mobilize donors and volunteers for the right federal candidates. The most persuasive voice to any candidate is a constituent's — especially a donor's. I hope to work with the DC Dems Statehood Committee to help identify the crucial races and mobilize Ward 1 Democrats to volunteer and donate. When they do, I'll encourage them to make clear why: "I'm supporting you because you support DC statehood."

Hold Democrats accountable. Rep. Eugene Vindman voted yes on all four anti-DC bills — the only VA/MD Democrat to do so — after DC residents knocked doors and donated to his campaign. We need to make clear there are consequences for that: no volunteer hours, no donations. And when we support candidates who stand with DC, we should say that too.

Prepare for the 2029 window. If the second Trump term plays out similarly to his first term, Democrats will retake Congress and the presidency in 2029. Last time that happened, the House passed HR 51 — but it died in the Senate because two Democratic senators wouldn't reform the filibuster. This time, we need to arrive with enough pressure already built that senators can't say no.
responses.congressResponse:
When Congress attempts to overturn DC laws or block our budget, my response will follow the same playbook that wins any political fight: organize locally, apply pressure federally, and reward allies while holding opponents accountable.

The most specific action I would take is mobilizing Ward 1 Democrats to reach out to people in their networks, asking them to contact their representatives directly. The most persuasive voice to any elected official is a constituent's. 

DC residents can't vote for members of Congress — but we can volunteer and donate to their campaigns, and we can make clear that we will or won't based on how they treat us. When Rep. Vindman voted yes on all four anti-DC bills after DC residents knocked doors for him, we got a painful lesson in what happens when we don't enforce that accountability.

Ultimately, the best defense against congressional interference is statehood. Every response to an attack on Home Rule is a band-aid. My goal is to make sure we're building toward the permanent fix at the same time we're fighting each battle as it comes.
responses.partners:
Free DC. This is my most important partner and the organization I'm most closely connected to. Free DC is a five-year statehood campaign that began in 2025 and is timed to capitalize on an expected Democratic trifecta in 2029. I've trained and volunteered with them, and I'm running for State Committeeman on the Free DC Slate alongside 40+ candidates for ward, at-large, and national seats. Kelsye Adams, a Free DC co-founder, is running for National Committeewoman on our slate. This is already a real working relationship, not a future aspiration.

Grow Democracy DC. Grow Democracy DC is a nonprofit born directly out of the Initiative 83 campaign — built by the same leadership team that ran one of DC's most successful recent ballot initiatives. I was a core part of that campaign, and those relationships are real and ongoing. Together, we collected enough signatures to get I83 on the ballot despite legal challenges and coordinated disinformation efforts, then won with nearly 73% of the vote — a supermajority in all eight wards and nearly 80% in Ward 1. That's the kind of organizing muscle that wins fights. Now that team is channeling those same skills into a broader democracy mission. The overlap with statehood is natural: if you believe DC residents should control their own elections, you believe DC residents should control their own laws and budget. Grow Democracy DC knows how to translate complex policy into a message that resonates with everyday voters, how to recruit and train volunteers at scale, and how to run a ground game that actually moves people. I'll work with them to bring that same energy to the statehood fight — identifying voters who care about democracy, giving them a clear path to get involved, and building the kind of sustained grassroots pressure that makes federal candidates pay attention.

DC Dems Statehood Committee. Since becoming a Ward 1 Precinct Representative, I attended my first Statehood Committee meeting in February and was so impressed — talented people with serious ideas, already running initiatives worth building on. The Committee is where I'll be able to work across all eight wards and coordinate with the broader party infrastructure in a way that no single outside organization can. There are many great local groups fighting for statehood, and that's a strength — but it also means we need a unifying force that can align all of them around a common strategy and timeline. That's what the DC Dems, at their best, can be. I'm running for State Committeeman because I believe the party is the right organization to bring these groups together and carry us across the finish line. The Statehood Committee won't be the loudest voice in that effort, but it may be the most important one — coordinating endorsements, mobilizing donors and volunteers for key federal races, and making sure that when the 2029 window opens, we're ready to move fast.
responses.voterInvolvement:
The key to involving DC voters and residents in the fight for statehood is meeting people where they are rather than expecting them to come to us. Most Ward 1 residents support statehood — it passed with nearly 89% support here in 2016 — but many don't know how to channel that support into action. My job is to build the on-ramps.

I learned this lesson on the Initiative 83 campaign. We didn't win by preaching to the already-converted at party meetings. We won by showing up at farmers markets, tabling outside grocery stores, working polling places on Election Day, and partnering with venues like Busboys and Poets that already had the trust and attention of the community. We met people in their neighborhoods and gave them something real to do. The same approach will work for statehood.

Concretely, I'll work through Ward 1's existing civic infrastructure — neighborhood associations, recreational sports leagues, religious groups, and local businesses — to host conversations about statehood that feel accessible, not intimidating. I'll make sure residents understand not just why statehood matters, but exactly how they can help: donating to a key congressional race, volunteering for a canvass, or simply calling their neighboring representative.

One thing I've learned from organizing is that people engage when they feel ownership over the fight. That means listening as much as talking — showing up to hear how being stateless is affecting people's lives, and letting those stories drive the message. The most powerful argument for statehood isn't a legal brief. It's a Ward 1 resident explaining what it actually costs them.
responses.additionalComments:
I want DC voters to know that for me, this isn't a stepping stone. It's not about building a political career or accumulating titles. It's about one thing: making DC the 51st state before I'm done.

That's why I've made a simple commitment to myself and to my neighbors: if I win and DC isn't a state by the end of my four-year term, I won't run for re-election. That opportunity should pass to someone with fresh energy and fresh ideas. I'm not interested in holding a seat for its own sake — I'm interested in winning statehood, and if I haven't delivered meaningful progress toward that goal, someone else should have the chance to try.

And if I don't win in June? I'll still be fighting. I'll continue serving as Ward 1 Precinct Representative, supporting our State Committee members, and doing everything in my power to advance the cause from that position. There is no version of this where I walk away. The fight for statehood is too important and too urgent.

What I hope DC voters take away is this: the window we've been waiting for is coming. A Democratic trifecta in 2029 could finally give us the chance to pass statehood — but only if we've done the work between now and then. Every election between now and 2029 matters. Every conversation, every donation, every volunteer hour matters. I'm committed to doing that work no matter what happens in June — but I'd sure love to do it as your State Committeeman.

responses.topThreeActions:
I have been serving as Co-Chair of Free DC's Congress Working Group for nearly a year, and in that time I have tracked dozens of legislative attacks on DC and directed hundreds of volunteers to call, email, and visit Congressional offices and attend hearings, creating a visible, vocal, sustained pro-Statehood presence on the Hill. I am incredibly proud of the persistence and dedication of our volunteers, the culture of learning and mutual trust that we have cultivated, and the incremental results we have achieved, creating allies among members of Congress and winning over reluctant Democrats.

Within Ward 1, I became a precinct representative for the Ward 1 Democrats last summer and joined the executive committee. In that role I have written resolutions condemning MPD collaboration with federal immigration enforcement and urging passage of the Safe Community Places and Policing Amendment Act that would strengthen our sanctuary city status. Pushing our local government to stand up to federal interference is a necessary step toward Statehood.

I am also extremely proud of joining the Free DC Slate, a diverse, energized, hardworking, optimistic crew of people who believe in a better future for all DC residents and will push the Democratic Party to work for the people and attain Statehood.
responses.intendedActions: I want Statehood to be part of the conversation every time a DC elected is speaking publicly. I would seek to increase funding and visibility for the DC Statehood Commission and a public education campaign around Statehood. I would also continue my work in Congress as detailed in other answers, and encourage all DC electeds to join in.
responses.congressResponse: I will continue to mobilize DC residents to loudly oppose any federal interference in our autonomy. As Congress Working Group Co-Chair, I have spoken to many DC residents who came to Congressional offices to lobby for the first time in their lives. Often, DC residents are made to feel that since we have no representation in Congress, we have no business going to the Hill. My position is that as soon as Congress introduces a bill or resolution that solely affects our local laws or money, then every member of Congress becomes our member of Congress. We should make it as painful as possible for Congress to continue to interfere in our local governance.
responses.partners: Of course I would continue to work with Free DC in my capacity as Co-Chair of the Congress Working Group. Our Shadow Senator Ankit Jain has been a close partner in our work in Congress, and I would seek to continue that partnership and grow relationships with any newly elected members of the shadow delegation. I would also encourage the Mayor and DC Council to become more vocal in promoting Statehood.
responses.voterInvolvement: I would encourage DC residents to consider themselves constituents of any member of Congress seeking to interfere in our local laws. I would also mobilize residents to demand that members of Congress cosponsor HR51/S51, the DC Statehood bill, and all other bills introduced that would grow our autonomy, such as HR5093/S2688, the pending bill that would place the DC National Guard under the control of our Mayor.
responses.additionalComments: In this moment, supporting DC Statehood is necessary and also not enough. We should be demanding that every DC elected oppose every attack on Home Rule. DC, being in a uniquely vulnerable position, is the bellwether for our democracy nationwide, and we need leaders who are willing to take on that challenge.

responses.topThreeActions: I have rapidly grown in my activism over the past year. I previously have volunteered for candidates for DC Council positions who supported DC Statehood and protecting Home Rule. Since August 2025, I have focused on increasingly larger leadership roles in Free DC through 1) a daily neighborhood noisemaking group going strong for eight months and counting, 2) installing dozens of DC flags at the Residences at Thomas Circle, 3) co-leading the Ward 2 Welcoming group, and 4) organizing participants for January 20th, MPD Oversight Hearing, No Kings, and soon-to-be May Day protests. I’m now taking the leap into party politics to use this organizing energy at a wider level.
responses.intendedActions: I expect to work closely with the rest of the Free DC Slate to amplify our voices in the Democratic party, which continues to ignore the strategic need to invest in DC Statehood. The Free DC Slate is a diverse group and we can use our various identities and partnerships to connect with others in the Democratic party leadership as well as throughout DC and the nation.
responses.congressResponse: DC has the benefit of being able showing up in person with little cost or notice. I will continue organizing to bring more residents to protests or participate in economic non-cooperation.
responses.partners: The biggest partner is Free DC, which is already collaborating with dozens of groups in strategizing, organizing, and delivering protests and actions. I am looking forward to growing relationships with unions to continue to strengthen the economic impact of our actions.
responses.voterInvolvement: DC voters believe their votes don’t count because others tell them they don’t. The Free DC Slate is united in its fight to make a DC Democratic Party that actually respects voters and wants to include them in the party processes. For those who don’t or can’t vote, their voice matters just the same. I am looking forward to leading community conversations to engage residents in non-cooperation actions to continue to make our collective impact felt.
responses.additionalComments: Protecting Home Rule and the status quo from authoritarianism is not enough – we need to fight for the full vision of a Free DC, which includes statehood. Free DC means freedom for all, without exception. I am committed and energized to be part of the movement that creates a Free DC for loved ones and neighbors.

responses.topThreeActions:
1) Attended several informational webinars and in-person workshops (Statehood Committee Monthly Meetings).
2) Attended several Emancipation Day Parades in support of DC Statehood.
3) I signed the DC STATEHOOD PLEDGE
responses.intendedActions:
1) Learn as much as I can about DC Statehood so I can be an informed ambassador to my community, to Congress, and to others who need to understand the history and importance of DC Statehood and Home Rule.
2) Host community seminars across Ward 2 to raise awareness and to educate residents on the history of the Home Rule Act and the benefits of statehood.
3) Work within the DC Democratic State Committee to inform the community and lobby Congress.
4) Work to Build National Coalitions: Focus on persuading Americans nationwide that DC’s lack of statehood is a democracy issue, encouraging them to contact their representatives.
5) Work alongside DC's shadow senators who lobby in other states and on Capitol Hill.
responses.congressResponse: 1) Collaborate with local partners to aggressively lobby Congress and push for legislative change to end disenfranchisement in DC.
responses.partners:
1) League of Women Voters. I have volunteered for several events and as an elected official, I plan to become more involved.
2) DC Women in Politics. I am a former member and plan to become a member again and get more involved.
responses.voterInvolvement:
1) Host seminars across Ward 2 to raise awareness and educate residents about DC Statehood and how and what they can do to support the movement.
2) Through my Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority, Inc. chapter, Xi Omega, provide awareness and information workshops so that members who reside in DC will be informed residents; and those who live outside of DC will also be equipped with information to share with their networks about the importance of DC Statehood and Home Rule.
responses.additionalComments: For a population of 700,000, larger than Vermont and Wyoming, it is essential to continue to fight for the right to representation in both the House and the Senate. It is our right!

responses.topThreeActions:
While I have been an activist for DC Statehood and self-determination since I was 18 years old, I have continued that work in recent years by proudly represented my national labor union on Capitol Hill advocating for DC Statehood, bringing the message to Senators and Representatives to that our union members in all 50 states are demanding DC Statehood.  

I have also worked with other national labor unions and national organizations to not just get a statement of support for DC Statehood, but to include Statehood in their official voting records and candidate interviews.  This harnesses the clout of national membership organizations with powerful political programs behind DC Statehood.  

Further, I have been an active member and Executive Board member of the Ward Three Democratic Committee.  The Ward Three Democrats have a robust Statehood Committee (which I am a member) and our highly effective Blue Wave Task Force, which supports pro-Statehood candidates across the country.
responses.intendedActions: We have built a beautiful constellation of groups in DC advocating for Statehood, all who are working diligently for our cause.  I have involvement and connections with a good many of these groups and I want to make sure the DC Democratic State Committee is working in concert with them and in support of them.  My own Ward Democratic organization's Statehood Committee and Blue Wave Task Force, the Capital Stonewall Democratic Club (DC's leading LGBTQ+ political organization of which I am a member and past president), our Woman's Democratic clubs (of which I am a member but my slatemates are both active leaders), and the labor unions (of which I have 40 years of involvement) are all groups for who I will work to see the DC Democratic Party is hearing from and working with towards our goal.
responses.congressResponse: When I first became involved with DC self-determination at age 18, we had a long list of supporting national organizations.  The list today is sadly much smaller.  But these groups have strong lobbying presences in Congress.  I believe they still care about DC self-government.  I want to continue my work to engage and mobilize them.
responses.partners: I have a 40 year career in the labor movement and know leaders in most of the national unions.  I have been a leader in the LGBTQ+ community as an officer of DC and national organizations. I also want to engage better the faith community, but will admit most of my fellow congregants are people without permanent legal status, so I will need help there.
responses.voterInvolvement: I don't buy the right wing lie that the people in DC don't support Statehood.  There is already amazing work being done by a wide variety of people and groups, many with great organizing skills and others with existing networks and communities.  I want to support their work and to make sure the Democratic Party supports them and works in concert with them.
responses.additionalComments: Don't get weary.  I have been active on this issue my whole adult life.  I believe we will see success.  Our movement is more powerful than it ever has been before.

responses.topThreeActions:
Over the past two years, I have consistently used my voice and platform to advocate for DC Statehood in both community and civic spaces. I have engaged in conversations with neighbors, colleagues, and local leaders to educate others about why full representation and autonomy matter for District residents.

I have also supported statehood-aligned candidates and initiatives through volunteer work and voter outreach, helping increase awareness and turnout in local and federal elections that directly impact DC’s path to statehood.

Finally, I have remained committed to staying informed and involved by attending meetings, participating in organizing efforts, and advocating for policies that strengthen local self-governance and protect the rights of DC residents.
responses.intendedActions:
As an elected official, I will center food access and economic dignity as core components of protecting Home Rule and advancing DC Statehood. My weekly volunteer work with Redelicious Food Co-op, where we rescue over 1,000 pounds of food from landfills and redistribute it while educating residents on preparing lesser-known foods, has shown me that local solutions work best when they are community-led.

I will advocate for policies that strengthen DC’s ability to fund and expand food access programs, support mutual aid networks, and protect locally driven initiatives from federal interference. Protecting Home Rule means ensuring we have the authority to meet our residents’ basic needs without outside obstruction. Advancing statehood is essential so we can fully control our budget, safeguard critical programs, and build a food system that serves all District families.
responses.congressResponse:
If elected, I will not be bullied or bought. I have a long history of speaking up and advocating for others, and that will not change in office.

When Congress attempts to overturn DC laws or block our budget, I will respond publicly and immediately. I will work with fellow elected officials to organize coordinated opposition, engage residents through town halls and public statements, and partner with advocacy organizations to apply legal and political pressure. I will also use every available legislative and procedural tool to defend our local authority.

Protecting DC’s laws and budget is about protecting the people who rely on them. I will stand firm in defense of Home Rule and the right of District residents to govern themselves.
responses.partners:
One key partner I intend to work with is Free DC. I support their mission to advance DC Statehood and protect Home Rule, and I value the organizing and education work they continue to lead across the District. I look forward to strengthening that relationship through active collaboration, public advocacy, and coordinated strategy.

I also intend to work closely with local mutual aid and food justice organizations, including Redelicious Food Co-op, where I volunteer weekly. These community-based groups understand firsthand how federal interference impacts residents’ daily lives. My existing relationships in these spaces allow me to connect statehood advocacy directly to real community needs.

In addition, I plan to partner with fellow DC elected officials and statehood-focused advocacy coalitions to ensure a unified, strategic approach to advancing full representation and protecting our local autonomy.
responses.voterInvolvement:
I intend to involve DC voters and residents by meeting people where they already are. Through my work in food distribution and community outreach, I have seen that conversations about statehood resonate most when they are connected to everyday realities like food access, housing, healthcare, and schools.

I will host community forums, attend neighborhood meetings, and use both in-person and digital platforms to educate residents about how the lack of statehood directly affects our budget, our laws, and our ability to meet basic needs. I will also create clear, accessible materials that break down what federal interference means in practical terms.

Most importantly, I will encourage residents to see themselves not just as voters, but as advocates. Protecting Home Rule and achieving statehood requires an engaged public, and I will work to build that engagement through transparency, education, and consistent communication.

responses.topThreeActions:
1.I’ve worked to elect over 50 lawmakers across the country who support statehood. Four of them are currently sitting on the Congressional committee which hosts hearings on all things home rule related. Two have gone on to become Governors. 
2. I worked with the DC Democratic Party to procure and implement and took that would allow them to quickly and easily develop a databases of DC Statehood supports across the country who are easily identifiable by state house and congressional district. 
3. I’ve elevated the unique challenges that the lack of statehood presents for residents of the District at four national conferences on education and disability rights and spent 5 days directly lobbying senators on the Hill and helped set up, prep, and manage 8 meetings with staffers.
responses.intendedActions:
I plan on continuing to elect democrats who not only support DC Statehood but know how to make this happen for us and are committed to the work. 
I’m going to make sure DC Statehood is the cornerstone of any and all democratic platforms going forward by working with other leaders of state democratic parties. 
Im going to continue to work with local issue based advocacy groups to lobby our elected leaders and explain why the lack of statehood impacts us all but especially veterans, people with disabilities, the elderly, the lgbtqia community, returning citizens and incarcerated friends family and neighbors, and our students and children.
responses.congressResponse:
1. Generate a letter people across the country can send to their Congressional leaders here to vote for DC statehood and autonomy and support our laws and budgets. 
2. Attend hearings and directly work with senate and congressional staffers to make sure they hear our stories first hand and cannot silence our voices. 
3. Work with national press and PR teams to make sure we get media coverage that ties the harms this overreach does to the lives that are directly impacted.
responses.partners:
DC Vote - volunteered and helped with lobbying days 
League of Women Voters- volunteered and have promoted their work both here and nationally in addition to partnering on events and panels 
National Stonewall Democrats: currently on the board and comms team
responses.voterInvolvement: By creating as many opportunities for people to engage, educated, and elevate volunteer opportunities, calls to action, events, campaigns and other activities in each and every ward across the city. It is my job to create strategic opportunities for our residents that meet them where they are with what they need.
responses.additionalComments: I was born and raised and have been impacted by the lack of statehood in various ways my entire life but I have never been more acutely aware of the dangers until now. My father is a Purple Heart veteran and has had a terrible time accessing the services and support he’s supposed to be getting. If he had Congressional representation he could get help from those offices but he has none. I have two kids with disabilities who are at risk of losing 504 accommodations and more. They have no one on the hill they can speak to about terrible vouchers would before their access to fair and appropriate education. I will never stop fighting for DC Statehood and I promise to do everything in my power to help others do the same.

responses.topThreeActions: As a Free DC organizer, I mobilized DC residents to lobby Congress against the proposed $1.1 billion cut to the District’s budget and other legislation undermining DC’s autonomy. I also helped organize consumer boycotts of Whole Foods and Target in response to their cooperation with ICE operations in the District. In addition, I serve as Free DC’s lead organizer engaging Washington Spirit supporters to raise public awareness about ongoing attacks on DC self-governance. As a result of this effort, more than 15,000 fans chant “Free DC” in the 51st minute of every home match, symbolizing our demand for DC to become the 51st state.
responses.intendedActions:
My approach to defending DC Home Rule is grounded in nonviolent resistance, solidarity, and political organizing. I believe we must refuse to normalize federal overreach by declining voluntary cooperation with federal agencies whose actions undermine DC’s self-governance and harm our communities. 

At the same time, I plan to build durable alliances with aligned movements and party partners across the country, so that once Democrats defeat the opposition in the general election, there is a coordinated national push to secure DC statehood and protect the District’s right to self-determination.
responses.congressResponse:
When Congress attempts to overturn DC laws or block our budget, I would push the Democratic Party to show up, visibly and publicly, alongside DC residents. 

Our party has been largely absent from the streets, and that needs to change. I would use the full organizing capacity of the largest political organization in the District to mobilize residents through coordinated town halls, mass call-in days, and nonviolent public actions that make clear DC will not quietly accept federal interference. 

One specific action I would take is organizing rapid-response mobilizations at key moments of congressional intervention, ensuring that attacks on Home Rule are met with immediate, citywide political pressure.
responses.partners:
I intend to work closely with organizations that have consistently and visibly defended DC’s autonomy, including Free DC, Harriet’s Wildest Dream, DC Vote, and the Fair Budget Coalition. I already have active relationships with several of these groups through organizing, coalition work, and joint mobilizations around Home Rule and budget autonomy, and I would build on that trust to better align party resources with movement-led efforts for statehood.

In addition, I would deepen collaboration with Advisory Neighborhood Commissioners, who are often on the front lines of defending local self-government. ANCs play a critical role in mobilizing residents, responding quickly to federal overreach, and grounding the statehood movement in neighborhood-level leadership.
responses.voterInvolvement: I intend to involve DC voters by treating them not just as supporters, but as organizers and leaders in the fight for statehood. Drawing on proven approaches used by Free DC, I would focus on giving residents real agency — equipping them with tools, messaging, and support to organize in their own neighborhoods, recruit their neighbors, and take local action.
responses.additionalComments: DC statehood will not be gifted from above — it will be won by the people who live here.

responses.topThreeActions:
1) Lead a ballot initiative (83) to improve our local democracy, free our vote, and open it to more voters - setting the stage for a strong democratic process leading up to Statehood
2) Participated in actions for Statehood with Defend DC and Free DC - one notably being an art build at Freedom Plaza in support of Statehood
3) Phone banked Pennsylvania and Texas Democrats to urge them not only to turn out to vote in the elections, but to also reach out to their representatives to support HR51
responses.intendedActions: It is a core message on our Free DC slate. I believe collective action over individual actions are more effective. As a DC Democratic State Committee member, I will organize within the groups/organizations that are already doing Statehood work, such as Free DC, DC Vote, 51 for 51; DC for Democracy; invite them to speak at our events; and citizen lobbying in the halls of power.
responses.congressResponse: As Congress has attempted to do this in the past, I protested/lobbied in the halls of power. I would go to national elected officials and urge them to protect our sovereignty.
responses.partners: Free DC, DC Vote, 51 for 51; DC for Democracy. Great relationships with all of the organizations I listed. I am an organizer and friend of many of the organizers in Free DC. My partner worked for 51 for 51 and has made meaningful connections with organizations across the country in support of DC Statehood, and I am deeply connected with the youth organizers; I've been to many DC Vote events and connected with their leadership in the past to support some of the pro-democracy work I've done (such as Initiative 83); and I am on the steering committee of DC for Democracy.
responses.voterInvolvement: We have to acknowledge that the fight for DC had been an arduous road. While we are facing high levels of voter apathy, we much also continue to make the case and fight for DC Statehood. And it's time to go beyond making the case for Statehood. It's a time where we embody Statehood and have our executive leadership wield a budget that puts power in the average person's hands, to give them purpose and meaning, and stop selling out our city to the highest bidder who give nothing back to us. When things feel the most stuck, is also when they are the most fragile. We are in a fragile time, and being prepared for statehood while it feels the most out of reach is paramount to achieving it when the time does come; because it will come. The last thing people want is to be preached at, so we will have to offer a vision that is irresistible of what the future can look like to mobilize and inspire people from all backgrounds. The first thing is centering conversation around food; and how we use food to convene, break bread, and discuss different topics together while making sure our basic needs are met. That is one of the ways to fight for Statehood.
responses.additionalComments: There are many things to prepare for, and one of them is having clarity and conversation around the State Constitution and imagine a future where we can co-create our future 51st State.

responses.topThreeActions: As a member of the DC Democratic Women’s Club, we routinely advocate for DC Statehood with the DC City Council as well as tapping into our social connections to support local groups in any Statehood efforts whether they are meetings, rallies or going to Capitol Hill to advocate directly with congressional members. On a personal level I educate and advocate for statehood in social circles and any clubs of which I am a member. And finally, the path to statehood lies in Congress and the pen of the POTUS. With that understanding I try to volunteer with as many national campaigns as possible through text banking, phone baking, and post carding to ensure we have a Statehood-friendly Congress and POTUS to increase the likelihood of achieving our goal.
responses.intendedActions: As a DC elected official, I will promote DC Statehood and protect Home Rule in any venue I am present as I believe deeply in these goals. If I can impact legislation in any meaningful way, I will seize the opportunity and convey that sentiment, in the strongest of ways, of the citizens of this great city that our destiny should be in our hands.
responses.congressResponse: Organize citizens and make Congress hear our collective voice. I believe in making oneself heard that is why I’ve had the Capital Hill switchboard number saved on my phone for years. I would organize call ins and visits to the offices of congressional members to demand DC’s autonomy remain intact and the wishes of the citizens, as conveyed to our City Council, be respected. I would work with DC’s Democratic leadership to engage fellow Dem’s across the country to advocate with their members of congress on our behalf.
responses.partners: To promote Statehood I will work with the city’s leadership structure, as well as groups who are organized and fighting for this cause. I have an existing positive rapport with many individuals in the District’s political environment which includes elected leaders and heads of pertinent organizations.
responses.voterInvolvement: I would involve DC voters through education, outreach and creating strategic partnerships. The current political environment has created a sense of urgency in many DC residents so it is incumbent upon those in impactful positions to organize that urgency into a focused, sustained effort to achieve Statehood.
responses.additionalComments: My family has been in DC since the end of the Civil War and we have seen many changes, fought and achieved civil rights and engaged the statehood fight in the early 80s. The notion of Statehood has been ingrained in me since I was a child. There has never been a more important time than now to make this stand. I have a strong voice, lion-like determination and I don't scare easily and I will fight for the people of DC until we are the 51st state.

responses.topThreeActions: I have participated in DC Statehood advocacy through my roles in Democratic politics, community leadership, and public statements emphasizing self-governance, home-rule, and full voting rights for DC residents. I took action as the former ANC 6A Commissioner and engaged in local governance that intersects with statehood discussions. I took action just last month hosting the Chocolate City Experience at Shanklin Hall in Adams Morgan. This event promotes the preservation of DC's culture and ensuring Dc natives voices are heard amid gentrification and federal control.
responses.intendedActions: I will organize events themed around Ward 6 priorities: Statehood means full local control over our community growth. Partner with Ward 6 fellow Democrats, Free DC, ANC, and groups like H street main street. I will advocate for a dedicated statehood/homerule working group or monthly agenda item. I will proposed DCDP resolutions or bylaws changes to prioritiz statehood education in Ward level GOTV.
responses.congressResponse: A specific action I would take is a public statement or op-ed that describes the issue as an attack on democracy and Ward 6 priorities, then call for concrete party action.
responses.partners: My top three partners include Free DC, I am a candidate on their slate and are friends with multiple members.I will work with my colleague Kelsye Adams at DC Statehood and LongLive GoGo. They make the voice of statehood louder than its ever been. I will partner with the office of the DC Delegate. I have a working relationship with our current Congresswoman as well as a few current candidates around public safety and small business support. The conversation on Statehood is aligned with our relationships.
responses.voterInvolvement: I intend to use grassroots outreach, education and entertainment to involve voters in the fight. By assuring the attendance or performances by nationally recognized figures like Taraji P Henson or James Taylor, we can expect large attendance and opportunities to register voters as well as promote statehood.
responses.additionalComments: Since 1973 DC has proven its ability to self-govern. Until Federal interference is obsolete we will continue to find discrepancies in our overall balance. It's time to make the declaration of independence whole by amending the constitution, naming Washington D.C the 51st state!

responses.topThreeActions:
I was a part of early Free DC organizing - I was on the Hill and spoke personally with Sen. Angus King to encourage him to prioritize the DC Local Funds Act and oppose the budget without it. I also went to many other offices and spoke with staff about it.

On May Day, I mobilized Free DC's presence at the May Day rally to build greater visibility with union allies.

I designed a canvassing program for Free DC's Ward 6 team that builds relationships and connects neighbors in Ward 6 to each other and to Free DC's efforts.
responses.intendedActions: We on the Free DC Slate intend to turn the DC Democratic Party into an organization that organizes the people's collective power and listens more closely to what DC residents need and want for their city. Through that engagement we can build solidarity and trust and have a people that is more ready to take action together.
responses.congressResponse:
We have to move fast and slow. Fast - when DC autonomy is violated, we have to mobilized people to rally and at a certain point take direct action.

Slow - we have to continually be building relationships and organizing our communities to be resilient and ready to keep turning out and to increase the number of people who turn out as well as the willingness to use collective power to compel the government to comply.
responses.partners:
Free DC - as noted I have strong connections to the campaign and as I am running on the Free DC Slate I expect those to deepen.
Faith Communities - I am a member of the New Synagogue Project and connected to organizations in the broader faith community through that membership. I've participated in many interfaith actions on different issues.
Unions - I am a union steward and connected to union staff through my work within Free DC as well as my membership in Metro DC Democratic Socialists of America.
responses.voterInvolvement: The Free DC Slate is running on a plan to renew the DC Democratic Party - to actively organize our communities, listen to their concerns, and defend our neighbors from federal overreach. In practice, this means relational organizing similar to the program I designed for Ward 6 Free DC. It means participatory mechanisms for public engagement. We can use the party budget to engage in real mass politics and build a movement that will stand united against this authoritarian.
responses.additionalComments: DC statehood is the tip of the spear for democracy in this country. Statehood is about autonomy and so many cities do not have autonomy under this competitive authoritarian regime or under state governments that do not represent them. DC Statehood is about equality and freedom - the promise of democracy - and we cannot stop at Statehood to ensure that promise is real for the generations to come. We need a third Reconstruction to bring about a true multiracial democracy - the kind that has not yet existed yet is in sight.
